title: general_name_matches: DER re-encoding for non-DN comparison
description:
Location: pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs, general_name_matches() (line ~1308-1326)

For non-DirectoryName GeneralName variants (URI, dNSName, rfc822Name, iPAddress, registeredId, etc.), the function encodes BOTH sides to DER via .to_der() and compares the resulting byte vectors:

  _ => match (a.to_der(), b.to_der()) {
      (Ok(a_der), Ok(b_der)) => a_der == b_der,
      _ => false,
  }

This is correct but allocates two Vecs on every non-DN comparison. These types have cheap-to-compare inner values (e.g., Ia5StringRef for URIs/dNSName, OctetString for IP addresses) that could be compared structurally using derived PartialEq or by matching on the same variant and comparing inner values directly.

What goes wrong: in the IDP/CDP distribution-point matching path (check_idp_dp_scope -> general_names_intersect), this is called O(m*n) times where m = |IDP names|, n = |CDP names|. Each call re-encodes both sides. For typical certs with 1-2 CDP entries this is negligible, but it is a hidden allocation in what reads like a comparison function.
